standard_prerequisites.name: The two relations
standard_prerequisites.statement: u close-epsilon v is the closeness relation generated along the constructors of the Cauchy reals, and u approx-epsilon v is the explicitly defined epsilon-approximation relation.

standard_prerequisites.name: Induction principles of the Cauchy reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a statement about closeness one may induct on its constructors, and to prove one about elements of RC one may induct on rational points and limits.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two inductions used in the two directions at source lines 1297 and 1301.

standard_prerequisites.name: Both relations are mere propositions
standard_prerequisites.statement: Each of the two relations is proposition-valued, so an equivalence reduces to a bidirectional implication.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction at source line 1296.

core_obligations: Reduce the goal to a bidirectional implication because both sides are mere propositions (source line 1296).

Left-to-right: induct on the four constructors of the closeness relation with the family C(u,v,epsilon) := (u approx-epsilon v); in each case u and v specialize to rational points or limits so that the definition of approx evaluates and the inductive hypothesis applies (source lines 1297-1299).
Right-to-left: induct on the Cauchy reals to assume u and v are rational points or limits, which lets approx evaluate (source line 1301).
Conclude by checking that the definitions of approx and the inductive hypotheses supply exactly the data of the relevant closeness constructors (source line 1302).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the equivalence to two implications.
Left-to-right by closeness induction on the four constructors.
Right-to-left by induction on the Cauchy reals.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Theorem 11.3.32 at source lines 1292-1294: for all u, v and positive rational epsilon the closeness relation and the epsilon-approximation relation coincide. The author's proof (source lines 1295-1303) is a two-direction argument in which the two directions use different induction principles and neither is a formality: after reducing to implications because both sides are propositions (line 1296), the left-to-right direction inducts on the four constructors of the generated closeness relation, and the point of the argument is that in every case u and v specialize enough for the explicit definition of approx to evaluate (lines 1297-1299); the right-to-left direction instead inducts on the Cauchy reals themselves so that approx evaluates, and then has to check that the definitions and the inductive hypotheses provide the data of the relevant closeness constructors (lines 1301-1302). The author remarks that this is an encode-decode pair, which the statement does not reveal.
